weighing.summary: The plan gives the head about 14:00 and the main body about 17:00. The record gives a spread over the afternoon. Sedgwick, testifying in 1864, put his own arrival at Gettysburg at about 2 p.m. Meade's dispatch to Halleck, headed 3 p.m., has the Sixth Corps 'just coming in', and his report says it arrived at 3; a major of the Third Division puts his regiment near the field about 3. Wright has the corps at Gettysburg about 4 and halting about two hours before it moved up to the left; Grant, Bartlett and Howe have brigades on the left about 5 and a little after. A dispatch of the time is the best class of writing, so the head is put at about 15:00; Sedgwick's 2 p.m. is one memory 281 days later, his own report of 1863 says only 'afternoon', and he found Meade out at the front, who rode out about 3 p.m. The window 15:00-17:00 shows the head, the corps at Gettysburg and the brigades on the left.
weighing.who: Meade commanded the army and wrote the dispatch at his headquarters; Sedgwick commanded the corps and testified about his own arrival; Wright and Howe commanded divisions; Grant, Bartlett, Kohler, Adams and Cowan commanded a brigade, a regiment and two batteries and give their own movements.
weighing.when: Meade's dispatch is of 2 July at 3 p.m. (his own hour). Kohler wrote 1 Aug, Grant 3 Aug, Bartlett 6 Aug, Wright and Howe 7 Aug, Sedgwick 8 Aug, Adams 14 Aug, Cowan 15 Aug 1863; Meade's report 1 Oct 1863; Sedgwick's testimony 8 Apr 1864.
weighing.where: The army headquarters was at the Leister house behind the cemetery; Sedgwick reports having gone there on arrival and found Meade out at the front. Wright's 'arrived' is at Gettysburg, where the corps halted; Grant, Bartlett and Howe date the arrival on the left, after the move up. These are two places and two moments, which is why the first arrival (about 3 or 4) and the 5 p.m. do not contradict each other.
weighing.how_knew: Meade saw the head come in and wrote it the same hour; Sedgwick's hour is his own recollection of his arrival; Wright, Grant, Bartlett, Howe, Kohler, Adams and Cowan state their own units' movements.
weighing.clock: All the witnesses are Union and no correction is applied (the plan's note of about 20 minutes between the armies' clocks plays no part here). 'About 2', 'about 3', 'about 4' and 'about 5' are read as plus or minus a quarter hour; Meade's '3 p. m.' is the hour of his dispatch.
weighing.independence: Meade's dispatch and report are one line (the lower end is flagged single_source where it stands alone). Sedgwick's testimony stands alone for 2 p.m. Wright and Adams (the artillery) are two reports for the 4 p.m.; Grant, Bartlett and Howe are three brigade and division commanders for the 5 p.m. and are independent of each other as reports, but the three brigades marched in one column. Kohler is a separate regiment.

source_panel_text: The Sixth Corps came in on Jul 2 after a march of about 35 miles: Meade's dispatch headed 3 p.m. has it 'just coming in', Wright puts it at Gettysburg about 4, and brigades reached the left about 5. Sedgwick's later memory of about 2 p.m. is the earliest hour and stays listed. Eight other values are listed.
